clue.text: A 'Special One' helping to produce body fluid

parts.note: 'a' in the sense of 'each' or 'for every' is PER, as in 'a pound a head'
the Roman numeral one is I
a ration is an allotted helping or portion

explanation.surface: José Mourinho, the self-styled 'Special One', lends a hand and works up a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special One' was the nickname of football manager José Mourinho, which makes the phrase look like one unit; here it splits into SP and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspiration is sweat, a fluid the body secretes through the skin.

clue.text: Choose an entrance for dictator and Spanish provocateur

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone dictating, speaking words aloud, so the phrase is what they would say

parts.note: to choose an entrance is to pick a door

explanation.surface: A tyrant is offered a choice of doors, and a Spanish agitator gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks like a tyrant, but it means a person dictating aloud, so 'pick a door' spoken gives the bullfighting word.
explanation.definitionFit: A picador is the horseman in a bullfight who goads the bull with a lance, a literal provocateur.

clue.text: Piece of music about infiltrating Republican Party

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A piece of music concerns someone working their way into the Republican Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting sections.

clue.text: With timely preparation, professional books inspiring film with nothing omitted

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so these pieces take the other one inside them

parts.note: PRO is short for professional
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

indicators.note: omitted says the letter for nothing is dropped from the film word

parts.note: a video is a recorded film
the letter O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A professional's books inspire a film, with nothing left out, all prepared ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' reads as motivating, but it means breathing in: the professional and the books take the shortened film inside them, and 'omitted' drops the zero-like letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A provident person makes provision for the future, preparing in good time.

clue.text: Rock and roll dance?

definitions.meaning: to ... is also to roll or whirl, as a ship ...
a lively Scottish or Irish dance

explanation.surface: A question about whether rock and roll counts as a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as rock and roll, a style of music, but the three words are separate definitions of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reel means to sway (rock), to lurch (roll) and is a folk dance.

clue.text: Propositions those desperate to introduce rock band

indicators.note: to introduce means to bring one piece in among the letters of another
desperate suggests things in a wild state, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: R.E.M. was an American rock band

explanation.surface: Desperate people propose bringing in a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' shuffles the clue word 'those' to THEOS, and 'to introduce' slots the band into it near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Theorems are propositions in mathematics or logic that are proved from axioms.

clue.text: Welsh girl shaving bottom following love letter

indicators.note: following says the next piece comes after the love letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: shaving the bottom removes the last letter of the down entry

parts.note: Megan is a girl's name popular in Wales

explanation.surface: A Welsh girl shaves her bottom after receiving a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaving bottom' trims the N from MEGAN; in a down clue the bottom is the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Excited at talk, pointlessly

parts.note: to witter is British slang for talking at length about nothing much

explanation.surface: Someone gets worked up while chattering on about nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' looks like it removes a compass point, but it belongs to the definition of WITTER, British slang for prattling on.
explanation.definitionFit: Atwitter means in a nervous flutter of excitement, like twittering birds.

clue.text: Gold transaction is nightmare

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: A deal in gold turns into a nightmare.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful, harrowing experience, a nightmare in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Are vocal expressions able to start to express language?

parts.note: can means to be able
tones are expressions conveyed by the voice

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A question about whether tones of voice let someone begin to express themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Tones fit the answer: Cantonese is a tonal language, so the surface hints at its own solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantonese is the Chinese language spoken in Guangdong and Hong Kong.

clue.text: Go into business half-cut

indicators.note: half-cut says only half the word is kept, its first half

parts.note: an enterprise is a business

explanation.surface: A tipsy person wanders into a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves ENTERPRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter a place is to go into it.

clue.text: Visit doctor and mostly express one's personal belief

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, losing its last letter

parts.note: to opine is to state one's opinion

explanation.surface: Pop round to see the doctor and air your own views.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to pay a casual, unannounced visit.

clue.text: One's wearing orange pants? Run!

indicators.note: wearing means one piece is clothed by the other, sitting inside it
pants is British slang for rubbish, poor, so the letters are in a bad, jumbled state

parts.note: one is I, so one's (one is) gives IS

explanation.surface: Someone sees a person in orange trousers and tells them to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but signals an anagram, giving ORGANE; 'wearing' then puts the one's piece inside it. 'Run!' is an imperative, matching the answer's form.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an event or business is to organise it; both are commands here.

clue.text: Stopped wanting Arab to be relaxed

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so these letters are missing

parts.note: arrested means stopped, as in arrested development
AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: An Arab, once detained, now wants to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has rested has had a break and is relaxed and refreshed.

clue.text: Farewell a son provided

parts.note: so long is an informal goodbye
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to a son, provided all goes well.
explanation.definitionFit: So long as is a conjunction meaning on condition that, the same as provided.

clue.text: Time to stop evil lasting forever

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so one piece fills the inside of the other

parts.note: immoral means wicked, evil

explanation.surface: Time is needed to put an end to an evil that seems to last forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Immortal means undying, never coming to an end.

clue.text: Rank Stones "close to perfection" in real life

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling, which off also means of food
scree is loose stones on a mountainside

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Rolling Stones members are ranked near perfect when away from the cameras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' suggests the Rolling Stones, but it is SCREE, the loose rock on slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Offscreen describes what happens away from film or television, in an actor's actual life.

clue.text: Pale bum certain to provide amusement

indicators.note: bum is British slang for bad or useless, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A pasty backside is sure to raise a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' reads as a backside, but as an adjective meaning faulty it shuffles PALE into PLEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or amusement, the feeling of being entertained.

clue.text: Maximum speed when horizontal?

definitions.meaning: something tilted fully over, a ..., ends up lying flat

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: tip an upright thing all the way over and it lies horizontal.
explanation.definitionFit: Full tilt is the idiom for top speed, from jousting knights charging with lances.

clue.text: Class times for George?

parts.note: a form is a school class
by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A question about which class someone puts George in.
explanation.walkthrough: George Formby was an English comedian and ukulele-playing singer of the 1930s and 40s.
explanation.definitionFit: Formby is the surname of entertainer George Formby, so George is a definition by example.

clue.text: Man perhaps follows American females into battle

indicators.note: follows says this piece comes after the others

parts.note: F is short for female; doubled, it is plural
Man Ray was an American artist, so Man is an example of a Ray

explanation.surface: A man follows some American women into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' seems to be any man, but Man Ray was the Surrealist photographer, so Man is one Ray.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl or fight, a small-scale battle.

clue.text: Run away from raid after youth initially displays thuggishness

indicators.note: after says this piece follows the initial letter
initially means just the first letter of the word is used
away from means this letter leaves the word that follows

parts.note: a robbery is a raid on a bank or shop
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A young thug runs from a robbery, showing his violent nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run away from' looks like fleeing, but it drops R from ROBBERY. YOBBERY is the behaviour of a yob, British slang for a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobbery is loutish, aggressive behaviour, the conduct of a thug.

clue.text: Cowboy from Oregon thrown out of introduction to radio presenter

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter
thrown out of says these letters are removed from the rest

parts.note: an anchorman presents a news broadcast
OR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Oregon

explanation.surface: A cowboy from Oregon is ejected from a radio presenter's introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranchman works on a cattle ranch, much as a cowboy does.

clue.text: Jeopardy host returned holding aquatic creature

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
holding says the clue words contain the letters, which run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The host of the TV quiz Jeopardy! comes back with a water creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'holding' into the definition, but it is the indicator that the letters are held inside 'Jeopardy host'; the definition is 'aquatic creature'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydra is a tiny freshwater polyp with tentacles, named after the many-headed Greek monster.

clue.text: Six-footer in mascara blushes

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside these clue words

explanation.surface: Someone with six-foot height wearing mascara blushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but insects have six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab is a dung beetle, and like all insects it has six legs.

clue.text: Accumulate in period prior to event

definitions.meaning: to ... a bill or debts is to accumulate them
the time leading to an event, such as an election

explanation.definitionFit: Run up is a phrasal verb for accruing, and as a noun the build-up period before something.

clue.text: State itself rejected after leader rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read backwards
leader rejected means the first letter is thrown out

parts.note: itself points to the clue's own word state, which is used as the raw material

explanation.surface: A nation is rejected after its leader is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'itself' refers to the word 'State': drop its leader to get TATE, then turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Etat is the French word for state, familiar from coup d'etat.

clue.text: Black Country is uninspiring

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a land is a country

explanation.surface: The Black Country, an industrial area of the English Midlands, is called dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is the old industrial area west of Birmingham, which makes 'Black Country' look like one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland means dull and unexciting, lacking anything to inspire.

clue.text: He put neat rum in to increase risk

indicators.note: rum means strange, so the letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A man pours undiluted rum into something, raising the stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but as an adjective meaning odd it scrambles HE PUT NEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To up the ante is to raise the stake in poker, hence to increase what is at risk.

clue.text: Hurry up, or skip a payment at work

indicators.note: at work suggests the letters are busy being reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: A boss tells someone to be quick, or else they'll miss a pay packet at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Make it snappy is an informal command to be quick.
